name: Haiku growth at a reasonable price
strategy: Rate-hiking cycle value rotation: concentrated financial sector exposure for net interest margin expansion, diversified value/defensive sectors, elevated cash for tactical deployment
reassessment_note: Post-FOMC rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% (first increase since 2023) creates clear policy regime shift. Previous 78% cash position was prudent pre-FOMC but is now excessive with interest rate trajectory clarity. Revised strategy deploys capital into rate-hike beneficiaries while removing underperforming TNA position (-9.75% loss, misaligned with mean-reversion thesis). Increased financial sector exposure (XLF 15%, JPM 8%) captures net interest margin expansion as banks benefit from wider yield curves and higher deposit costs justify passed-through rate increases. Maintains defensive value/dividend characteristics through energy (XLE), healthcare (XLV), and broad value (VTV) while keeping modest crypto hedge (BTC, ETH) for diversification. This creates intentional portfolio differentiation from parallel Round 2 (growth/AI infrastructure focus) with <1% overlap (only BTC-USD), satisfying Round 3 novelty constraint. Rate-hiking environment historically favors financials and value sectors where this book is concentrated, opposite to Round 2's growth orientation.

positions.thesis: Financial sector ETF captures core rate-hike thesis; widened net interest margins from 3.75%-4.00% fed funds rate directly expand bank earnings. Rising rate environment supports continued rate hikes through 2027 (markets pricing 4 more moves). XLF provides diversified exposure to regional banks, money center banks, insurance, and diversified financial services rather than single-name concentration risk.

JP Morgan premier financial franchise with significant rate sensitivity; investment banking and trading revenues expand in volatile markets, lending margins widen. Capital-strong position enables continued share buybacks and dividend growth. JPM historically outperforms in early hiking cycles as funding costs remain stable while lending rates rise immediately.

Energy sector demonstrates resilience in higher-rate environment; hyperscaler capex for AI infrastructure ($650B+ 2026 guidance) supports steady oil demand while energy valuations remain attractive. Energy's commodity-linked cash flows provide inflation hedge and contrast with financial-heavy positioning.

Healthcare sector defensive characteristics provide steady dividend income and lower rate sensitivity than growth; sector has lagged but provides portfolio ballast. Healthcare earnings less cyclical to macro conditions, providing downside protection while maintaining exposure to aging demographics and innovation themes.

Broad value ETF captures systematic mean-reversion opportunity as valuations normalize in higher rate environment; low P/E multiples and high dividend yields favor value factors over growth. VTV provides diversified value exposure across sectors, avoiding Round 2's growth concentration.

Biotech sector has experienced significant valuation compression and significant underperformance; smaller weighted position captures mean-reversion opportunity in healthcare innovation and patent-protected therapies. Stop-loss at -15% protects against continued deterioration while maintaining upside capture if sentiment normalizes.

Goldman Sachs direct exposure to investment banking revenues (M&A, capital markets) and trading businesses benefits materially from higher rates and increased market volatility. Direct financial name provides rate-hike leverage and trading-cycle upside complementary to XLF diversified basket. Stop-loss protects against earnings disappointment.

Bitcoin maintains contrarian hedge positioning against broader value-equity portfolio; cryptocurrencies provide diversification during equity market dislocations. Stop at -25% and take-profit at +150% manages volatility while capturing potential upside if macro regimes shift.

Ethereum provides technology-ecosystem diversification; contrarian positioning captures potential upside if crypto recovers while limiting losses to -25%. Take-profit at +100% locks in gains on recovering valuations. Diversifies away from pure financial/value concentration.
